transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Um, I came in because... well, for the past few weeks, I've felt this heavy, sad pressure just sitting on me almost all day. Even when I'm at work, you know, smiling at my patients and trying to do my job, inside I feel like I'm barely holding myself together.
Have you ever felt this way before, or is this the first time you've experienced a period like this?

No, um, I don't think so. This is really the first time I've experienced anything quite like this. I mean, I've had bad days or felt stressed before, but never this... this constant, heavy feeling that just won't go away. So, yeah, this is the first time.
Did anything specific happen in your life, like a major change or a stressful event, right around the time these feelings started?
Yeah, actually. Um... I found out I was pregnant. This whole thing started shortly after that. So it's been going on for about three weeks now, just right after I got the news.
Do you feel that these symptoms are primarily a reaction to the news of the pregnancy, or are you feeling this way regardless of the life change?

Um, I'm honestly not really sure. I mean, the timing definitely lines up with finding out, but... I don't know if it's just a reaction to the news or if I'd be feeling this way regardless. It just sort of hit me all at once right after I got the news, so it's hard for me to separate the two.
Are you experiencing any physical symptoms, such as significant changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or persistent physical fatigue, that feel different from typical pregnancy symptoms?

Well, my appetite is definitely off. I know I should be eating regularly, um, especially now, but most days food just sounds completely unappealing to me. I'll actually realize halfway through a clinic shift that I've only had crackers or maybe a coffee all day. I just don't have the drive to eat right now, which I know isn't good.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns since you found out you were pregnant?
Um, not really, no. I mean, I'm tired, but I think I'm still sleeping about the same amount as I usually do. I haven't noticed any big changes there.
Are you still finding enjoyment or pleasure in the hobbies and activities you usually like to do?

Not really, no. Usually, after my shifts, I used to paint, or go to yoga, or maybe do some salsa dancing to decompress. But lately... I just go straight home and sit on the couch. I've even been ignoring my texts, because honestly, none of it feels worth the effort right now.
Do you find yourself feeling a sense of worthlessness or feeling guilty about the fact that you aren't feeling happy about this pregnancy?

No, not really. I mean, I know I'm not feeling the way people expect you to feel about a pregnancy, but I don't really feel guilty about it. It just is what it is right now. And I don't feel worthless, either... I just don't feel much of anything about the whole thing.

When you think about the news of the pregnancy, do you feel that it is a situation that you are struggling to cope with or adjust to, or does it feel like a separate, overwhelming weight that has settled over you regardless of the news itself?

I think it feels more like a separate weight. That's actually why I came in to see you. For the past few weeks, I've just felt this... this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me almost all day long. It doesn't really feel tied to the news of the pregnancy itself. Even when I'm at work, you know, smiling at my patients and doing my job, inside I just feel like I'm barely holding myself together.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead or that you might want to hurt yourself?

Well, yeah. That's actually what scared me enough to say something about it at my prenatal appointment. I don't have a plan to actually hurt myself or do anything like that. But... I have been having these thoughts lately where I just wish I wouldn't wake up.
Have you noticed if your movements or speech have slowed down, or conversely, have you felt physically restless or unable to sit still lately?

Yeah, it's definitely the first one. I haven't been restless at all, but everything I do just feels slowed down. It's... it's kind of like I'm moving through syrup. Even simple things at the clinic, like gathering wound supplies or finishing up my charting, it all just takes me noticeably longer than it should.

Are you still able to manage your daily responsibilities at work and at home without significant assistance, or has the 'slowed down' feeling made it impossible for you to keep up with your normal routine?

I'm still managing to get to work, but it's definitely getting harder to keep up. Like I said, I'm slower, and... well, my supervisor actually pulled me aside the other day because my charting has been incomplete. At home, I'm just... I'm pulling away from my friends, and I don't have the energy for the things that usually keep me steady. So I'm doing it, I guess, but not very well.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or staying focused on your tasks since these feelings started?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's like my brain just feels really foggy lately. At work, I'll catch myself rereading the same medication orders or wound-care notes over and over because it just isn't sinking in. And making decisions... things I normally do on autopilot just make me freeze up now. I just stand there and second-guess myself constantly.
Are you able to function at all in your role at the clinic, or do you feel that your symptoms are currently preventing you from performing your work duties entirely?

Well, like I mentioned a minute ago, I am still making it to work, so it hasn't stopped me entirely. But I wouldn't say I'm functioning well. My supervisor has already noticed the incomplete charting, so it's definitely affecting my job. And outside of the clinic, it's the same thing... I've been pulling away from my friends and the things that usually keep me steady. So I am still functioning, I guess, but just barely.
Have you been experiencing any experiences where you see, hear, or believe things that others around you do not seem to notice or share?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I don't see or hear things that aren't there, and I don't have any strange beliefs or anything. It's really just the low mood and the fog and... the lack of energy. But no, nothing like what you're asking about.
